params.body:
Closes #25

## Why

A prospect asked whether youth trends can be read for Flanders or for Belgium. They cannot: the finest region that holds Belgium is Benelux, and the country code `be` is one of its spellings. An engine that is handed the regions and asked for the most specific one for a Belgian signal has no narrower answer to give, so a Belgian and a Dutch signal are stored alike. The country is not lost on the way; it is never asked for.

## What

Standard 0.19.0, added only:

- `region-belgium`, `region-netherlands` and `region-luxembourg`, each `broader: region-benelux`. A reading tagged with one still counts for Benelux and for Europe, as every nested region does.
- The spellings move with them: `be`, `nl` and `lu` match the country, and each country carries its own names (België, Belgique, Nederland, Holland, Luxemburg).
- Flanders, Wallonia and Brussels are spellings of Belgium, not regions.

## Choices

- **No Flemish region yet.** Whether a Belgian signal is Dutch- or French-language is its language. Belgium with a language gives a Flemish and a French-speaking reading without a third level. A later release adds the regions when the counts say Belgium alone is too coarse.
- **All three countries, not Belgium alone.** With only Belgium under Benelux, "Benelux" would come to mean "the Netherlands, probably", and a Dutch signal could not be told from one about the three together.
- **Nothing is re-tagged.** What was tagged Benelux stays Benelux and is found under it together with the new tags.

## Changed in practice

An engine that reads the regions from the Standard starts tagging the three countries where a signal shows one, and Benelux only for what is about the three together. A count per region that does not roll a child up into its parent will show Benelux shrink as the countries appear.

How well a model tells a Belgian from a Dutch signal in Dutch-language text without a place name is not measured here; a sample after the pipeline takes this version should say.

## Checked

- `npm run check`: standard ok. `npm run export`: exports regenerated.
- `npm test`: 103/103, including the region spellings (the three codes now answer the countries, ten spellings added) and compatibility with every earlier release.

## After merge

Tag `v0.19.0`, then take it into the pipeline with `bin/sync-standard.mjs` (a pull request there). Only signals classified after that carry a country.
params.title: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg are regions under Benelux (0.19.0)
